First, let's rewrite the polynomial equation in the form ${P}_{n}(x)=0.$ To do this, we subtract all the terms from the right-hand side so that the right-hand side becomes $0:$

$$
\begin{aligned}3{x}^{3}-{x}^{2}+5x-2 & =-2+5x \\ 3{x}^{3}-{x}^{2}-2 & =-2 \\ 3{x}^{3}-{x}^{2} & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Next, notice that all of the terms of the polynomial have a common factor of ${x}^{2}.$ We can factor out the ${x}^{2}$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}3{x}^{3}-{x}^{2} & =0 \\ {x}^{2}(3x-1) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, by applying the zero product rule, the solutions are $x=0,$ and $x=\frac{1}{3}.$
